## Abundance: Adult Data
There are four common terrestrial land cover types in our study area: broadleaved woodland, improved grassland, arable and suburban.

What trapping effort is sufficient to detect a difference in mosquito abundance between these different habitat types?

### Available data
https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/jvec.12137  
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13071-025-06975-w
Medlock 2015 used mosquito magnet baited with octenol so likely undersampled Cx pipiens
Rough estimates: 
Widlake: 1.5x more Cx.pp in rural vs urban, mean c. 5pernight (but note BG Lure used)
Medlock 2015: < 1 to 18 in grassland pernight (using moz magnet and octenol), all spp
Wet woodland - Aedes most common - 30-40/night, Cq richardii c. 12 per night - min x12 difference

### One run before simulating many times
First set up study design options

```{r}
points <- st_read(here(".//QGIS//waterbodiesClippedRamsar500bufferwithFragAndMajLC.shp"))
# split points into quartiles by mca
points$mcaq <- with(points, cut(menCrAr, 
                                breaks=quantile(menCrAr, probs=seq(0,1, by=0.25), na.rm=TRUE), 
                                include.lowest=TRUE))
```

```{r}
# create dataset 
days <- 1:4                                      # number of days at each area per month
traps <- 1:3                                   # traps set per day per habitat type
habitat <- c("wood","grass","suburban","arable") # most common land cover types
area <- LETTERS[1:4]                             # 4 Ramsar sites

moz.data <- expand.grid(traps=traps,habitat=habitat,days=factor(days),area=area)

mcaQ1 <- sample(points$menCrAr[points$mcaq %in% "[0,0.0381]"],length(moz.data$area)/4)
mcaQ2 <- sample(points$menCrAr[points$mcaq %in% "(0.0381,0.115]"],length(moz.data$area)/4)
mcaQ3 <- sample(points$menCrAr[points$mcaq %in% "(0.115,0.326]"],length(moz.data$area)/4)
mcaQ4 <- sample(points$menCrAr[points$mcaq %in% "(0.326,13.6]"],length(moz.data$area)/4)


moz.data$mca[moz.data$habitat %in% "wood"] <- mcaQ4
moz.data$mca[!moz.data$habitat %in% "wood"] <- sample(cbind(mcaQ1,mcaQ2,mcaQ3))

moz.data$row.id <- factor(paste("row", 1:nrow(moz.data), sep = ""))

```

```{r}
hist(moz.data$mca)
```

Assume effect sizes
```{r}
mca <- 1.5

bwood  <- 5  
suburb <- 3   
grass  <- 2
arabl  <- 0.5
```


Simulate abundance using GLMMMisc
```{r}
moz.data <-
  sim.glmm(
    design.data = moz.data,
    fixed.eff =
      list(
        intercept = log(3),   
        habitat=log( 
          c(wood=bwood        
            ,suburban=suburb
            ,grass=grass
            ,arable=arabl)
        )
        ,mca=log(mca)
        ),
    rand.V =               
      inv.mor(             
        c(area=1.1
          #,days=1.1
          )),              
    distribution = "poisson")   
```

See what the simulated data looks like
```{r}
ggplot(moz.data) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x=habitat,y=response))
```

Fit a model
```{r}
moz.pois <- glmer(response ~ habitat + (1|area), family = "poisson", data = moz.data)

output <- summary(moz.pois)
output
cfs <- output$coefficients
#exp(cfs)
```

## Simulate many times

Write a function which does the above
```{r}

pwrFunc <- function(...){
  library("GLMMmisc")
  library("lme4")
   
  
  # create dataset                                       # number of days at each area per month
  traps <- 1:ntraps                                     # traps set per day per habitat type
  habitat <- c("wood","grass","suburban","arable") # most common land cover types
  area <- LETTERS[1:4]                             # 4 Ramsar sites
  days <- 1:3
  moz.data <- expand.grid(traps=traps,habitat=habitat,days=factor(days),area=area)

  mcaQ1 <- sample(points$menCrAr[points$mcaq %in% "[0,0.0381]"],length(moz.data$area)/4)
  mcaQ2 <- sample(points$menCrAr[points$mcaq %in% "(0.0381,0.115]"],length(moz.data$area)/4)
  mcaQ3 <- sample(points$menCrAr[points$mcaq %in% "(0.115,0.326]"],length(moz.data$area)/4)
  mcaQ4 <- sample(points$menCrAr[points$mcaq %in% "(0.326,13.6]"],length(moz.data$area)/4)


  moz.data$mca[moz.data$habitat %in% "wood"] <- mcaQ4
  moz.data$mca[!moz.data$habitat %in% "wood"] <- sample(cbind(mcaQ1,mcaQ2,mcaQ3))

  moz.data$row.id <- factor(paste("row", 1:nrow(moz.data), sep = ""))
  
  moz.data <-
  sim.glmm(
    design.data = moz.data,
    fixed.eff =
      list(
        intercept = log(5),   
        habitat=log( 
          c(wood=bwood        
            ,suburban=suburb
            ,grass=grass
            ,arable=arabl)
        )
        ,mca=log(mca)
        ),
    rand.V =               
      inv.mor(             
        c(area=areaRand
          ,row.id = 1.2
          )),              
    distribution = "poisson")  
  
  #fit glmm
 moz.pois <- lme4::glmer(response ~ habitat + mca + (1|area) + (1|row.id), family = "poisson", data = moz.data)
  
  output <- summary(moz.pois)
  cfs <- output$coefficients
  grass <- cfs[2,4]
  suburban <- cfs[3,4]
  arable <- cfs[4,4]
  mca <- cfs[5,4]
  
  pvalgrass <- 0
  pvalsuburban <- 0
  pvalarable <- 0
  pvalmca <- 0

  if(length(output$optinfo$conv$lme4$messages)==0){
    if(grass<=0.05){pvalgrass<-1}
    if(suburban<=0.05){pvalsuburban<-1}
    if(arable<=0.05){pvalarable<-1}
    if(mca<=0.05){pvalmca<-1}
  }
  return(c(pvalgrass,pvalsuburban,pvalarable,pvalmca))
}

```


Run in parallel
```{r}

mca <- 1.1

bwood  <- 5   
suburb <- 1    
grass  <- 2
arabl  <- 0.5

areaRand <- 1.2

ntraps <- 3

cl <- makeCluster(detectCores()-1)               # get cores from your computer - 1
clusterExport(cl, varlist=c("pwrFunc","ntraps","points","mca","bwood","suburb","grass","arabl","areaRand"),
              envir=environment())               


start <- Sys.time()
sim.res <- parLapply(cl,1:1000,pwrFunc) 
stopCluster(cl)   # stop the clusters
end <- Sys.time()
end - start

```

Calculate power to detect a difference
```{r}
l <- do.call(rbind,sim.res)
l2 <- rowSums(l)

# Power
length(l2[l2==4])/1000*100
```

```{r}
              envir=environment())

end <- Sys.time()
end - start

# Power

}
```

```{r}
dat <- cbind.data.frame("traps"=rep(1:10,3)
                        ,"power"=c(sc1pwr,sc2pwr,sc3pwr)
                        ,"scenario"=c(rep("S1",10)
                        ,rep("S2",10)
                        ,rep("S3",10)
                        ))
```

```{r}
ggplot(dat) +
  geom_point(aes(x=traps,y=power,col=scenario)) +
  xlab("Number of traps per habitat type per area") +
  ylab("Power (%)")
```
